chunks: What al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Fadalah and Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mu'awiyah ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

If a man performs nine circuits between al-Safa and al-Marwah, then let him continue on one and discard eight. And if he performs eight circuits between al-Safa and al-Marwah, then let him discard them and restart the sa'y. And if he begins with al-Marwah, then let him discard what he has performed and begin with al-Safa.

key_terms.أَشْوَاطٍ: circuits or laps performed in the ritual movement
key_terms.تِسْعَةَ: nine, referring to an excessive number of circuits
key_terms.ثَمَانِيَةَ: eight, referring to an invalid count requiring recommencement
key_terms.ٱلسَّعْيَ: sa'y, the ritual going back and forth between al-Safa and al-Marwah
key_terms.ٱلصَّفَا: al-Safa, the hill from which sa'y must begin
key_terms.ٱلْمَرْوَةِ: al-Marwah, the hill paired with al-Safa in the rite of sa'y

ai.seo_question: What should someone do if they perform more than seven circuits of sa'y between al-Safa and al-Marwah?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about mistakes in sa'y between al-Safa and al-Marwah during hajj or 'umrah. It explains how to correct extra circuits and clarifies that the sa'y must begin from al-Safa.
